organizations.normalization_notes: Military assignments and civilian employment remain distinct. USS Raleigh is preserved as the assignment named by the source rather than treated as a civilian employer.
The 1940 magazine masthead names the company and William T. Dewart Jr. as secretary. Do not merge it with The New York Sun, Inc. or with the elder William T. Dewart's offices.

affiliations.role_title: Specialist first class; later assigned to OSS field radio operations
affiliations.date_precision: Day-level entry into Navy and initial OSS assignment dates as reported to the May 1944 board
affiliations.research_notes: The board explicitly dates Navy entry before OSS assignment and matches the unusual indexed name and specialist rating. Neither the board nor the index identifies a civilian employer. The University of Wisconsin was a recruitment setting, not an employer or established student affiliation.

affiliations.date_precision: Documented on the dated 18 May 1940 masthead; the beginning, end, and pay terms of the office are not established
affiliations.research_notes: The primary masthead explicitly differentiates William T. Dewart, president and treasurer (father), from William T. Dewart Jr., secretary. A separate OSS section history calls the major a New York Sun publisher in 1944, but this does not prove Munsey was his immediately preceding employer, that the Sun and Munsey were the same legal employer, or that his secretaryship was paid.

claims.claim_text: A May 1944 OSS board record identifies the indexed Mike Devyak as a U.S. Naval Reserve specialist assigned to OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The board gives the unusual full name, the same specialist first-class rating, Navy service, and explicit OSS assignment. The index has no service number to cross-check.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence: distinctive full name, matching indexed Navy specialist rating, and a contemporary OSS assignment; Box 184 remains unreviewed.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Navy entry and OSS assignment dates establish military sequence, but no earlier civilian employer is named.
claims.match_notes: Do not label the University of Wisconsin as employer or student status merely because the board says he was recruited there.

claims.claim_text: Mike Devyak entered the U.S. Navy in February 1943 and was assigned to OSS in August 1943; Navy service is his documented pre-OSS pathway.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The contemporary board entry explicitly supplies the two dates and identifies him as USNR. It does not name a Navy unit before OSS or a civilian employer.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from distinctive name, exact specialist rating, and contemporary OSS context.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit sequence: entered Navy 17 February 1943; assigned OSS 23 August 1943.
claims.match_notes: Military assignment is kept distinct from civilian employment.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Major William T. Dewart Jr. matches the OSS Morale Operations officer named in a wartime section history.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The OSS history names the same full name, suffix, rank, and OSS branch and also calls him publisher of the New York Sun. The corporate masthead independently distinguishes him from his father.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from exact name and suffix, major's rank, OSS context, and separate father-versus-son role evidence; original Box 184 personnel file is unreviewed.
claims.temporal_assessment: The 1945 history discusses 1944 OSS activity and does not date Dewart's exit from civilian publishing.
claims.match_notes: The 1940 Sun and Munsey mastheads name the elder Dewart as president/publisher; his offices must not be assigned to the indexed son.

claims.claim_text: A 1940 Frank A. Munsey Company magazine masthead lists William T. Dewart Jr. as the company's secretary.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The contemporaneous masthead prints the publishing company and explicitly separates the son's secretary title from the father's president and treasurer titles.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from exact full name and suffix, corroborated by the OSS history's major of the same name and newspaper-publishing role.
claims.temporal_assessment: Dated 18 May 1940: certainly pre-OSS, but not established as the final civilian post or immediate predecessor to OSS.
claims.match_notes: A company secretary role is documented; paid employment is not established. Do not equate the separate Frank A. Munsey Company and The New York Sun, Inc. legal entities without proof.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Carl L Dewald has a high-confidence match to an official Army enlistment entry of the same name.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Army bulk entry agrees with the NARA index on name and a protected unique identifier. An occupation code is not a named employer.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from protected identifier and full name; Box 184 file remains unreviewed.
claims.temporal_assessment: Wartime enlistment supports identity, not a particular pre-OSS employer or transfer date.
claims.match_notes: No speculative civilian workplace is assigned from the Army occupation code.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Colonel Andre DeWavrins resembles Free French intelligence chief André Dewavrin (Colonel Passy), but their identity is not established.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The index's unusual similar name and colonel rank fit a public biography, while the official French history does not identify an OSS personnel file, Box 184, or shared archival identifier.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Ambiguous: similar name plus colonel rank are suggestive but insufficient to merge the indexed person with Colonel Passy.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Free French biography cannot be used to assign this index row a pre-OSS employer or military assignment without an identity bridge.
claims.match_notes: Keep the NARA printed DeWavrins spelling and the DGSE Dewavrin spelling separate. Request Box 184 file before any identity promotion.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The NARA row names Sgt Cornelis Devries in Box 184. Exact and de Vries variant searches did not produce an independently linked OSS person; same-name genealogy and school records lack an OSS bridge.
person_updates.next_action: Review Cornelis Devries's Box 184 file for service identity, civilian work and OSS assignment.

person_updates.identity_evidence: A public legal-career trail exists for Henry P. de Vries, including a later FARA legal-counsel listing, but it has no shared wartime identifier or direct OSS Box 184 link. The indexed Henry P Devries is not assigned that career.
person_updates.next_action: Compare Henry P Devries's Box 184 file with the lawyer candidate and establish dated pre-OSS work only after an identity bridge.

person_updates.identity_evidence: Contemporary OSS board entry has Mike Devyak's distinctive full name, the same Navy specialist rating as the index, Navy-to-OSS dates and wartime branch context. The source does not name a civilian employer.
person_updates.next_action: Review Mike Devyak's Box 184 file for the last civilian employer before Navy entry and any direct Navy unit before OSS assignment.

person_updates.identity_evidence: Only the indexed Nicholas DeVyner name and Box 184 are established. Vyner/de Vyner surname results do not tie a contemporary person to OSS or an employer.
person_updates.next_action: Review Nicholas DeVyner's Box 184 file for identity, name variants and immediate pre-OSS affiliation.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The NARA index documents Gwendolyn J Dew in Box 184, but exact-name and institutional searches yielded no independently linked wartime identity; a different Dorothy Gwendolyn Dew is not this person by name alone.
person_updates.next_action: Review Gwendolyn J Dew's Box 184 file for her identity, personnel status and prior employment or occupation.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The official Army bulk entry matches Carl L Dewald's indexed full name and a protected unique identifier. It does not identify a named employer or establish the Army-to-OSS date.
person_updates.next_action: Review Carl L Dewald's Box 184 file for pre-service employer and military-to-OSS chronology.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The index and a wartime OSS section history agree on the full William T. Dewart Jr. name, suffix, major rank and OSS role. A 1940 Munsey masthead separately names the son secretary and the father president/treasurer.
person_updates.next_action: Review William T Dewart Jr.'s Box 184 file for recruitment date, final civilian employer and exact relationship between the Sun and Munsey publishing roles.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The indexed Andre DeWavrins has a colonel rank and resembles André Dewavrin, Colonel Passy. Official French sources establish Passy's Free French intelligence career but do not connect him to the indexed OSS Box 184 personnel file.
person_updates.next_action: Review Andre DeWavrins's Box 184 file before assigning Colonel Passy's BCRA career or changing the indexed spelling.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The index names Ralph A DeWeese in Box 184. Search results for a later physician and commercial people-finder entries provide no shared wartime identifier or OSS file linkage.
person_updates.next_action: Review Ralph A DeWeese's Box 184 file to establish identity and earlier occupation or employer.

person_updates.identity_evidence: An artist named Robert K DeWeese served in wartime military service, but no source checked ties him to Box 184. An OSS medic named Robert DeWeese lacks the indexed middle initial, and a separate indexed Robert C DeWeese Jr. has a distinct row; these identities remain separate.
person_updates.next_action: Review Robert K Deweese's Box 184 file against artist and medic candidates without merging it with adjacent Robert C DeWeese Jr.
